advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an auto-fire note to the `concurrency` catalog line in code-review-base.md, matching the sibling content-triggered overlays (deletion-impact, surface-parity).
evidence: code-review-base.md adds: `- \`concurrency\` — threads, async tasks, multiprocessing, locks, channels, shared/global mutable state, file/DB locking.` (no auto-fire parenthetical)

The sibling `deletion-impact` line reads `...(this overlay also fires automatically on such diffs).` and `surface-parity` reads `...(this overlay also fires automatically when a write-surface adapter file changes).`

registry.py marks the entry `"concurrency",  # (content-triggered) threads/async/multiprocessing/locks/channels — races` and content_triggered_overlays fires it: `if _has_concurrency_token(diff_text): fired.add("concurrency")`
advisory.finding: The `concurrency` catalog entry in code-review-base.md omits the '(this overlay also fires automatically on such diffs)' note that its sibling content-triggered overlays carry, despite the overlay being content-triggered per registry.py.
advisory.suggested_fix: Append '(this overlay also fires automatically when the diff touches synchronization primitives).' to the concurrency catalog line.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a negative-control test asserting a `Popen`-only diff (no included token) does NOT fire `concurrency`, plus at least one more excluded-family token (e.g. `.lock`, `Promise.all(`).
evidence: Commit/ticket: excluded '...async/await, bare `fork`, `retry`, `.lock`, `Popen`, `Promise.all(`, `setInterval(`, `select {` — that noisy tier is project-overlay material'
Recall test line: "+    subprocess.Popen(cmd, start_new_session=True)" — contains both excluded `Popen` and included `start_new_session`
Only negative control for the excluded family: test_async_await_only_diff_does_not_fire_concurrency (async def/await)
registry.py:369-410 _CONCURRENCY_TOKENS omits Popen/fork/retry/.lock deliberately — no test asserts these do NOT fire
advisory.finding: The deliberate EXCLUSION of the `Popen` token family (a core precision property the commit and ticket both assert) is never verified. The recall test's diff line `subprocess.Popen(cmd, start_new_session=True)` carries both the excluded `Popen` and the included `start_new_session`, so if `Popen` were mistakenly added to `_CONCURRENCY_TOKENS` no test would fail; the only negative control for the excluded family covers async/await.
scenarios: A future edit accidentally adds `Popen` (or `Promise.all(`, `select {`) to the token tuple, silently degrading the high-precision guarantee, and the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix:
Add: def test_popen_only_diff_does_not_fire_concurrency(): assert "concurrency" not in reg.content_triggered_overlays('--- a/p.py
+++ b/p.py
@@ -1 +1,2 @@
+    subprocess.Popen(cmd)
') — and similar for other excluded tokens.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a table-driven test that parametrizes over each `_CONCURRENCY_TOKENS` entry and asserts a minimal added-line diff containing it fires `concurrency`.
evidence: tests only supply diffs containing `start_new_session` (recall) and `sync.Mutex` (removal)
No table-driven parametrization over the token tuple exists in tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py
advisory.finding: Of the 40 tokens in `_CONCURRENCY_TOKENS`, only two distinct tokens (`start_new_session`, `sync.Mutex`) are exercised by any test. The remaining ~38 committed tokens (e.g. RwLock, Semaphore, flock, O_EXCL, make(chan , FOR UPDATE, SKIP LOCKED, atomic., pthread_) have no positive-recall assertion, so a typo or accidental deletion of any of them would not fail the suite.
scenarios: A refactor mistypes or drops a token (e.g. `RwLock`→`Rwlock`); the recall property for that token silently breaks with no failing test.
advisory.suggested_fix:
@pytest.mark.parametrize("tok", reg._CONCURRENCY_TOKENS) with a diff `"--- a/f
+++ b/f
@@ -1 +1,2 @@
+  " + tok + "
"` asserting `concurrency` fires.
